title: Level 2 Biology — Life Processes at the Cellular Level (2025)
subject: biology

questions.text:
Photosynthesis is essential for sustaining life on Earth. It provides the organic molecules and oxygen that most ecosystems depend on. The rate of photosynthesis can be influenced by several environmental factors and varies considerably between different habitats.

In New Zealand, native rātā-kāmahi forests grow in moist western regions where rainfall is abundant and temperatures are moderate. By contrast, some coastal dune grasses must photosynthesise in exposed environments with intense sunlight, salt-laden winds, and sandy soils that drain rapidly.

Discuss the process and importance of photosynthesis to plants, and how environmental factors can influence this reaction in both rātā-kāmahi forest and coastal dune grass environments.

In your answer, include discussion of:
- the process of photosynthesis, including details of the main stages and the role of chlorophyll
- why the rate of photosynthesis changes throughout the day, and how factors such as light intensity and water availability influence this variation
- why coastal dune grasses may have lower rates of photosynthesis during the hottest part of the day compared to rātā-kāmahi forest plants in sheltered inland locations.
questions.expectedAnswer: Photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2. Light-dependent reactions occur on thylakoid membranes using chlorophyll to absorb light. Light-independent reactions occur in the stroma. Subalpine tussock plants may close stomata during peak heat to conserve water, limiting CO2 intake and reducing photosynthesis rate.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved (A3-A4): Describes the process of photosynthesis; the light-dependent phase as occurring in the thylakoid/grana; the light-independent phase as occurring in the stroma; the change in light intensity during daylight hours; the effect of water availability; why CO2 is needed for photosynthesis; what is meant by a limiting factor; the role of chlorophyll. Merit (M5-M6): Explains the light-dependent phase and where it occurs; the light-independent phase and where it occurs; changes in rate of photosynthesis due to light intensity; changes in rate due to water availability; why stomatal closure in hot conditions limits photosynthesis in tussock plants. Excellence (E7-E8): Provides detailed discussion of the key phases of photosynthesis, locations, and linked to the context; changes in rate of photosynthesis due to a combination of factors; why coastal dune grass plants may show reduced photosynthesis during peak heat compared to sheltered rātā-kāmahi forest plants.

questions.text: Mitochondria are the organelles responsible for generating most of a cell's supply of ATP. Name and describe the location of four key structures of a mitochondrion.
questions.expectedAnswer: 1. Outer membrane — smooth outer boundary of the mitochondrion. 2. Inner membrane — folded membrane inside the outer membrane. 3. Matrix — the fluid-filled interior space. 4. Cristae — folds of the inner membrane that increase surface area.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: At least three structures named and described correctly.

questions.text:
The longfin eel / tuna (Anguilla dieffenbachii) is a native freshwater eel species endemic to New Zealand. Longfin eels are ambush predators that rest concealed among submerged logs and rocks for extended periods before striking at passing prey with a rapid burst of speed.

Discuss where and when anaerobic and aerobic respiration occur in the longfin eel.

In your answer, include discussion of:
- anaerobic respiration and aerobic respiration in the eel's cells, and identify where each type of respiration occurs in an animal cell
- why the longfin eel can carry out anaerobic respiration for only short periods of time during a predatory strike
- the advantages and disadvantages of the longfin eel carrying out both anaerobic and aerobic respiration.
questions.expectedAnswer: Anaerobic respiration occurs in the cytoplasm, producing small amounts of ATP quickly without oxygen. Aerobic respiration occurs in the mitochondria, producing larger amounts of ATP but requiring oxygen. During a predatory lunge, muscles work faster than oxygen can be delivered via the gills and bloodstream.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved (A3-A4): Describes aerobic respiration; anaerobic respiration; anaerobic occurring in the cytoplasm; aerobic occurring in the mitochondria; anaerobic being used during intense bursts of activity; aerobic being used when oxygen is available; an advantage of aerobic OR anaerobic; a disadvantage of aerobic OR anaerobic. Merit (M5-M6): Explains aerobic respiration and its advantages and disadvantages; anaerobic respiration and its advantages and disadvantages; the process of anaerobic respiration/glycolysis including its location; the process of aerobic respiration including its location; functions of the various parts of the mitochondria. Excellence (E7-E8): Provides detailed discussion of anaerobic respiration and how the advantages and disadvantages directly relate to the longfin eel; aerobic respiration and how the advantages and disadvantages directly relate to the eel; why the eel needs BOTH systems to function effectively in its lifestyle as an ambush predator.

questions.text:
Changes in temperature can significantly affect the activity of enzymes, thereby influencing the rate of all cellular processes in an organism.

Discuss the importance of enzymes in cellular processes, and how temperature affects enzyme activity.

In your answer, include discussion of:
- the structure of enzymes
- the role of enzymes in biological processes
- the mechanism by which enzymes function
- why high and low temperatures have different effects on enzyme activity compared to the optimum temperature.

You may include diagrams to support your answer (optional).
questions.expectedAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of proteins. They have a specific 3D shape including an active site. Temperature affects the kinetic energy of molecules and the shape of the active site, thus influencing enzyme function.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved (A3-A4): Describes the structure of enzymes; function of enzymes as biological catalysts; lower activation energy; catalyse biochemical reactions; tolerance limits of enzymes; enzymes denaturing at extreme temperatures; optimal temperature described; reduced reaction rate outside optimal temperature; the lock and key model OR the induced-fit model. Merit (M5-M6): Explains how the structure of enzymes enables them to work; the lock and key model or induced fit model; why extreme temperatures affect the rate of activity of enzymes; the formation of the enzyme-substrate complex; the role of enzymes in a biological process. Excellence (E7-E8): Provides detailed discussion of the function of enzymes related to their structure and why temperature affects them; the effects of high and low temperatures on the rate of enzyme activity; the impact of enzyme activity on the rate of cellular activity in an organism.
